chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Eat the oil, and massage with the oil, for it is from a Blessed tree'.

key_terms.الزَّيْت: Oil (specifically olive oil in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of olive oil in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith through a chain linking Imam al-Sadiq to the Prophet, emphasizing the olive tree's status as a 'blessed tree' (*shajarah mubarakah*). This narration not only validates the medicinal and culinary virtues of olive oil but also reinforces its spiritual significance as a symbol of divine light and purity in Shia tradition.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Al Qaddah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Eat the (Olive) oil, and massage with the (Olive) oil, for it is from a Blessed tree’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad al-Ash‘ariy from ibn al-Qaddah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘Use Olive oil for food and rubbing; it is from the blessed tree.’
Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from ibn al-Qaddah from abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has narrated from a similar Hadith.”
